description: How a Snowflake semantic view is read. `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` lists the views a selection reaches, and `SYSTEM$READ_YAML_FROM_SEMANTIC_VIEW` returns each one's specification as YAML. What the reader takes from that YAML is what the model is offered: the public members it can query, the variables it must bind, the tables the view depends on, and the prose that becomes first-touch and retrieval context. Both packages read the same YAML into the same model, so an agent sees the same view whichever package built it.

show_rows.description: Rows of `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` and the views they list. Drivers report the column names in either case, every column but the name, namespace, and comment is ignored, and a blank or null comment is no description.

cases.name: lower-case keys, and a blank comment is no description
upper-case keys, and a null comment

specifications.description: A view's id, its YAML specification exactly as Snowflake returns it, and the model read from it. `description` is the comment `SHOW SEMANTIC VIEWS` reported, used when the YAML has none. Entries may be a list or a mapping keyed by name. Members marked private are dropped, `labels` containing `filter` (in any case) marks a dimension or fact usable as a named filter, and a member's type is its `data_type`. A base table's database, schema, and table are SQL identifiers: a quoted one is exact, with doubled quotes undone, an unquoted one is upper-cased, and a missing database or schema is the view's own. Dependencies are complete only when every table names one and there is at least one. `expected` is either the model, or `unsupported` with the reason when a variable has no bindable type.

cases.name: a parameterized view in the list form Snowflake returns
cases.yaml:
name: ORDERS_PARAM_MODEL
description: "Orders, with a threshold variable."
variables:
  - name: MIN_TOTAL
    description: Only orders whose total is at least this amount count.
    data_type: "NUMBER(10,2)"
    default_value: "0"
tables:
  - name: ORDERS
    base_table:
      database: ANALYTICS
      schema: PUBLIC
      table: '"orders"'
    facts:
      - name: ORDER_TOTAL
        expr: '"order_total"'
        data_type: FLOAT
        access_modifier: public_access
    metrics:
      - name: TOTAL_ABOVE_MIN
        description: Sum of order totals at or above MIN_TOTAL.
        expr: SUM(orders.order_total)
        access_modifier: public_access

metrics.name: TOTAL_ABOVE_MIN
metrics.description: Sum of order totals at or above MIN_TOTAL.

MIN_TOTAL.description: Only orders whose total is at least this amount count.

cases.name: members: private ones dropped, time dimensions read as dimensions, top-level metrics have no parent
cases.yaml:
name: revenue
description: Revenue model.
tables:
  orders:
    base_table:
      database: ANALYTICS
      schema: PUBLIC
      table: ORDERS
    dimensions:
      region:
        description: Sales region.
        label: Region
        data_type: VARCHAR(16)
        synonyms: [territory, area]
      secret:
        access_modifier: private_access
    time_dimensions:
      ordered_at:
        data_type: TIMESTAMP_NTZ
        comment: When the order was placed.
    metrics:
      order_count:
        description: Orders.
      hidden_count:
        access_modifier: PRIVATE
metrics:
  - name: total_revenue
    description: Revenue.
    synonyms: sales

cases.name: filter labels mark facts and dimensions, and named filters are context only
cases.yaml:
custom_instructions: Use booked revenue for finance questions.
module_custom_instructions:
  - Use booked revenue for finance questions.
  - Exclude test orders.
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {database: ANALYTICS, schema: PUBLIC, table: ORDERS}
    dimensions:
      - name: active_only
        labels: filter
        description: Active orders.
    facts:
      - name: amount
        description: Order amount.
        labels: [Filter, finance]
      - name: cost
        access_modifier: private_access
      - name: discount
    filters:
      - name: recent_only
        description: Recent orders.
    metrics:
      - name: revenue
relationships:
  - name: orders_to_customers
    left_table: orders
    right_table: customers
    relationship_columns:
      - left_column: customer_id
        right_column: id
      - left_column: region
        right_column: region
  - from_table: orders
    to_table: regions

expected.name: REVENUE_MODEL

cases.name: base tables are SQL identifiers: quoted kept exact, unquoted upper-cased
cases.yaml:
tables:
  - name: lines
    base_table:
      database: '"Commons"'
      schema: live
      table: '"order ""lines"""'
  - name: lines_again
    base_table:
      catalog: '"Commons"'
      schema: LIVE
      table: '"order ""lines"""'

cases.name: a base table without a namespace inherits the view's own
cases.yaml:
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table:
      table: orders

cases.name: a base table without a table name leaves the dependencies incomplete
a view with no tables has no complete dependencies
typed variables keep a safe declared SQL type and coerce defaults
cases.yaml:
variables:
  - name: region
    data_type: VARCHAR(16)
  - name: since
    data_type: DATE
    default_value: "2024-01-01"
  - name: include_test
    data_type: BOOLEAN
    default_value: "TRUE"
  - name: limit_rows
    data_type: number(10, 2)
    comment: Upper bound.
  - name: odd
    data_type: "TIMESTAMP_TZ(9) WITH SPACE"
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {table: ORDERS}

cases.name: an unsupported variable type makes the view unsupported
cases.yaml:
variables:
  - name: payload
    data_type: VARIANT
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {table: ORDERS}

expected.unsupported: Snowflake semantic parameter "payload" has unsupported type "VARIANT".

cases.name: a variable without a type makes the view unsupported
cases.yaml:
variables:
  - name: payload
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {table: ORDERS}

expected.unsupported: Snowflake semantic parameter "payload" has unsupported type "missing".

cases.name: a blank description is no detail, even beside a label
cases.yaml:
tables:
  - name: orders
    base_table: {table: ORDERS}
    facts:
      - name: amount
        description: ""
        label: Amount
      - name: tax
        label: Tax

sql_types.description: A variable's declared type and the SQL type its bound value is cast to, or null when the declared text is not safe to splice into SQL: letters and underscores, optionally followed by a precision and scale.
